does: Coats thin strips of meat in a mix of soy, wine and starch and a little oil before a fast stir-fry, so that they stay silky and juicy.
how: Cut the meat across the grain into thin slices, then thin strips.
Mix it with a little soy sauce and rice wine until the liquid is taken up.
Stir in a little cornflour until each strip is lightly coated, then a little oil to keep the strips apart.
Leave it a short while, then stir-fry it fast in hot oil.

cues.text: The strips feel slick and lightly coated, with no pool of liquid.
The cooked strips look smooth and glossy, not shrunken and grey.

mistakes.mistake: Adding too much starch, which turns into a gummy coat.
mistakes.fix: Use just enough to coat each strip thinly.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving out the oil, so the strips clump in the wok.
mistakes.fix: Stir in a little oil last.

variant_of.differs: The marinade is short and holds starch and oil, which form a thin coat that keeps fast-cooked strips silky.
